rappel_detail.pull: Built for a single 60 m rope, and the stations were placed to give steep, clean pulls clear of the gully.
rappel_detail.notes: First of three fixed rappel stations equipped in recent years on the South Arete; single 60m rope is sufficient for each rap.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed bolt/chain station, climber's right of the summer gully/chimney
hazards: One party found one of these bolted stations placed on a large block that is not attached to the mountain: counted from the bottom it is the third, which with three stations in place is this top one, above the gully. Inspect the rock the bolts are in, not only the hardware, and back it up if you are not satisfied.
The short 5th-class step above the station is exposed with real fall consequence. Stay roped, and place gear on it rather than soloing down.
rappel_detail.station: Top station of the rappel line North Cascade Mountain Guides installed after the June 2022 rockfall: bolts and chains on a big ledge immediately above the small tree that older parties used to sling. All three new stations sit climber's right of the gully and off the line of ascent — skier's left as you face out on the way down — deliberately taking the descent out of the gully feature the route climbs. You reach it by downclimbing the arete's 3rd/4th-class ground plus one short, exposed 5th-class step.

rappel_detail.pull: Steep and fairly clean on a 60 m rope, provided the strands are kept out of the gully when you throw.
rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the arete; short easy downclimbing sections connect stations.
hazards: The gully immediately beside the line is the loose ground that produced the 2022 rockfall. Keep ropes and feet out of it — that is the whole reason this rappel line was moved.
This is a very popular route and stations back up on summer weekends; anything knocked loose lands on the party waiting below.
rappel_detail.station: Second of the three chain-and-bolt stations, on the ledge just above the chockstone, again set off to the side of the climbing line. Short sections of easy downclimbing link it to the station above, and how much you rappel versus downclimb is a party choice.

rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel returns to the base of the route.
hazards: Talus and slabs immediately below the last station, with the pull zone directly above anyone still coiling ropes.

The alternative descent some parties take instead — traversing to the Southwest Couloir and walking it out — avoids rope work but is loose and can hold firm snow well into summer, so it is not automatically the safer option without an axe.
rappel_detail.station: Lowest chain station. The rappel from it returns you to the base of the route, where the climbers' trail leads back down through talus and slabs alongside the stream to the Blue Lake Trail.

set.rappels: 3 single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope from bolted chain anchors on the South Arete descent, each under 30 m, with easy downclimbing between them
